_why: John, 12 Oct 2026: on a few passages, readers (Jewish and Christian, or within each) divide over meaning, and tN gives one side or none. These are the one place Yada needs human writing: John or a trusted reviewer writes a fair note giving two or three readings. Until an entry has a note with status 'approved', the reader sees nothing extra and the report flags the passage. In every listed passage, no summary sentence comes from the disputed verses. 'question' is the candidate's subject, for John's list only; it is never shown. Option 3 (John, 12 Oct): instead of prose, John fills 'positions' with two or three readings, each at most 18 words, optionally naming who holds it ('held_by', e.g. 'many Jewish readers'). The app sets them in the Readers differ sentence. Set 'status' to 'approved' when done. Where tN already gives readings, those show meanwhile (option 1). 'kind' (John, 12 Oct): 'data' shows only the JPS 1917 verse (Old Testament) or the manuscript fact; 'tn-readings' shows tN's readings (verse notes, or a chapter introduction that sets out two readings) meanwhile; 'positions' shows nothing until John approves positions; 'held' shows nothing. Each position may carry 'source' (e.g. 'Tyndale Open Study Notes, JHN 6:53-58'), credited under Sources. Positions (John, 12 Oct, supersedes 'note' and the 18-word form): each position is a source's own sentence, unchanged, with 'source' (e.g. 'Tyndale Open Study Notes') and its own 'status'; John approves or rejects each and writes nothing. 'held_by' only where the source's own words say it. Two or more approved positions show; a passage with no source stating two views moves to kind 'held'.
